text: In ischemic stroke, SD is frequently observed as peri-infarct depolarizations (PIDs), which serve as a principal mechanism driving infarct expansion into penumbral areas. In hemorrhagic stroke subtypes like aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), secondary injury significantly influences both early brain injury and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI), the latter being a major contributor to stroke-related morbidity and mortality. Thus, a thorough analysis of SD dynamics is fundamental for developing effective neuroprotective strategies in stroke care.
source_label: Spreading depolarization in neurocritical care: a review of SD’S pathophysiological continuum and clinical translation
